Maintenance Report — MNT-0128-003

Asset: WELL-0128 (NE-07 Well 128, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 05 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 May 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 17 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0128-0029 on 2023-05-04 Report written: 07 May 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0128-0029 at 11:30 on 2023-05-04 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.9% of the pad area, estimated 4.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 278 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 222 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0128-003 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.44% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

The thermal reading at inspection INS-0128-0038 showed the wellhead at 35.7 °C with the air at 36.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0128-0044 showed the wellhead at 39.2 °C with the air at 33.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. Maintenance Report — MNT-0128-015

Asset: WELL-0128 (NE-07 Well 128, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 19 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 22 May 2024 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 77 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0128-0082 on 2024-05-16 Report written: 24 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0128-0082 showed the wellhead at 35.0 °C with the air at 29.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started, but it was not written down (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0128-0143 at 13:45 on 2025-07-31 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.3% of the pad area, estimated 2.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0128-027

Asset: WELL-0128 (NE-07 Well 128, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 16 Sep 2025 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 578 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0128-0146 on 2025-08-21 Report written: 18 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0128-0146 showed the wellhead at 32.7 °C with the air at 33.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0128 (NE-07 Well 128, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 11 Sep 2026 08:00 · Finished: 12 Sep 2026 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 24 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0128-0198 on 2026-09-10 Report written: 13 Sep 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0128-0198 at 08:00 on 2026-09-10 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.2% of the pad area, estimated 1.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 4.6 hours after the inspection. Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.
